entries.relevance_notes: Explicitly attested as legatus Aug. pro praetore of Arabia in 193 and 194 AD.

Ael. Severia[nus] Max[i]mus III 14150^6, Ael. Severianus Maximus III 14172. 14174; nomina plus minus mutila in ceteris miliariis.
segments.offices_and_career: Legatus Aug. pro praetore provinciae Arabiae t. 1, a. 193 Pertinace imperium obtinente... item a. 194 imperante Septimio Severo... Consul designatus etiamtum legatus Arabiae t. 1, consul suffectus circa a. 194; ὁ λαμπρότατος ὑπατικός t. 2. Severianum post consulatum legatum provinciae Thraciae fuisse viri docti e titulo 2 filio Perinthi dicato collegerunt (cf. Stein Thracia p. 39 sq.), dubito num iure; fieri potest ut oriundus fuerit Perintho.

segments.prosopographical_commentary: The author doubts the hypothesis of Stein and other scholars that Severianus was legatus of Thrace after his consulship, which was inferred from an inscription dedicated to his son in Perinthus.
segments.bibliography_or_cross_references: IGR 1, 794 = Jahresh. 23 B. 171, 118 (2); CIL III 14149^43, 14150^6, 14172, 14174, 13612, 14169, 14170^3, 14176^4, 13614; Thomsen Die röm. Meilensteine d. Prov. Syria, Arabia u. Palästina passim; Stein Thracia p. 39 sq.

governorship_factoids.exact_text: Legatus Aug. pro praetore provinciae Arabiae t. 1, a. 193 Pertinace imperium obtinente... item a. 194 imperante Septimio Severo... Consul designatus etiamtum legatus Arabiae t. 1
notes: Attested on multiple milestones in Arabia under Pertinax (193) and Septimius Severus (194).

Von A. Stein erschlossen: Ehreninschrift Perinth (IGR I 794 = AEM VIII 217,43) fuer den Sohn A 261 nennt den Vater lamprotatos hypatikos (vir clarissimus consularis); da A 260 Statthalter von Arabia (193/194, praetorisch) und hier Konsular ist, verwaltete er Thracia (konsularisch) nach Arabia. Erschlossen, nicht direkt bezeugt.

career_factoids.exact_text: Consul designatus etiamtum legatus Arabiae t. 1, consul suffectus circa a. 194
notes: Designated consul while still serving as governor of Arabia.
